en: The *Sūtra on the Nature of the Vajrasamādhi Being Pure, Indestructible, and Imperishable*, Spoken by the Buddha;
the translator’s name is lost, now appended to the *Records of the Three Qin*.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Gabled Hall of the Great Forest Monastery in the kingdom of Vaiśālī,
together with a great assembly of five thousand bhikṣus, including the Venerable Mahākāśyapa and the Venerable Śāriputra.

Together with eighteen thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who were well-known to the assembly, such as the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana and the Venerable Mahākātyāyana, their names being: Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
Brahmadatta Bodhisattva, Prabhāsaśrī Bodhisattva, Jyotiḥśrī Bodhisattva, and Siṃharāja Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattvas— Siṃhagarbha, Gadgadasvara, Gandhahastin, Vajradhvaja, Vimukticandra, Sumerudhvaja,
and the Mahāsattva Maitreya— were all such preeminent leaders as these.

Furthermore, there were the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Wisdom-Virtue, Star-Virtue, Constantly Adorned, Universal Radiance, Samantabhadra, Full Moon, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Wondrous Sound, Space-Treasury, and Pure Sound; together with these and others, there were eighteen thousand Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas. They were accompanied by countless sons of heaven from the realms of Brahmā, Śakra, and the World-Protecting Kings, as well as the Dragon Kings Nanda and Upananda, along with four great dragon kings and their retinues of hundreds of thousands of dragons, each holding a king of wish-fulfilling jewels to make offerings to the Buddha.

The Gandharva King, the Asura King, the Garuḍa King, the Mahoraga King, and the Great Powerful Ghost King, each accompanied by immeasurable retinues, offered hard black aloeswood and sandalwood from the ocean’s shore, along with various blended incenses, as offerings to the Buddha.

In another direction, there was a Brahmā King named Viśāṃpati, who, together with ten thousand Brahmās including Manojña and Jālinīprabha, held celestial *mandārava* flowers and *mahāmandārava* flowers and scattered them over the Buddha and the great assembly. The exquisite celestial flowers scattered by the Brahmās were soft, fresh, and brilliant, most delightful to behold; they transformed above the Buddha into a floral canopy, manifesting radiant adornments upon the multi-storied lecture hall, appearing like the seven-jeweled ornamentation of a pure land.

At that time, the World-Honored One emerged from the vihāra and proceeded to the Dharma seat; he spread out his own sitting mat, sat down cross-legged, and entered the samādhi of the cessation of mental activity, remaining unmoving in body and mind.
Emerging from the Samādhi of the Extinction of Thought, he enters the Samādhi of the Lion’s Roar Mind.
Emerging from the Samādhi of the Lion’s Roar Mind, he enters the Samādhi of the King of the Lion’s Boundless Agility.
Emerging from the Lion’s Vigorous Display Samādhi, he entered the Great Radiance King Samādhi.
Emerging from the Great Radiance King Samādhi, he entered the Great Compassionate King’s Mark Samādhi.
Arising from the Great Compassionate King’s Mark Samādhi, he enters the Samādhi of the Perception of Unconditioned Loving-kindness.
Arising from the Samādhi of the Perception of Unconditioned Loving-kindness, he enters the Samādhi of Superior Intentional Loving-kindness.
Emerging from the Samādhi of Supreme Benevolence, he enters the Samādhi of Great Emptiness.
Emerging from the Samādhi of Great Emptiness, he enters the Samādhi of Suchness.
Emerging from the Samādhi of Suchness, he enters the Samādhi of the Mark of Liberation.
Arising from the samādhi of the mark of liberation, he enters the samādhi of the indestructible and unextinguishable king.
Arising from the samādhi of the indestructible and unextinguishable king, he enters the vajra samādhi.
Emerging from the Vajra-samādhi, he entered the Great Emptiness Nirvāṇa-mark Samādhi.

At that time, the World-Honored One arose from these various samādhis and emitted light from his entire body; the light was like clouds, entering the Buddha’s face and emerging from the crown of his head. It stood in the void like a vajra-banner, universally illuminating the great assembly and the multi-storied lecture hall of Vaiśālī with the color of white jewels.

When the entire great assembly beheld this sign, Maitreya immediately rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, circumambulated the Buddha seven times, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet with his right knee touching the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
For what reason has the Tathāgata, the Great Sage, today entered this supreme samādhi, such that his radiance is even more manifest than ever before?
He must surely intend to preach for the sons of the Dharma kings the dharma-kingdom, the stage of the dharma-king, and its practices.
How does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abide in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi?
By what adornments, by what skillful means, and by cultivating what wisdom does he attain abiding in the Vajra Samādhi, thereby achieving *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?

At that time, when the great assembly heard Maitreya Bodhisattva ask the Buddha about this meaning, they were all greatly rejoiced and, with one voice and in different mouths, praised Maitreya Bodhisattva:
“Excellent, excellent!”
“O Dharma Prince!
You are indeed able to ask the Buddha about such a great meaning.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well!
I shall now analyze and explain for you the dharmas of the stages of merit practiced by Bodhisattvas."

The Bodhisattva of the first stage is like the new moon; although its radiance is not yet manifest, its luminous characteristics are entirely complete. The Bodhisattva of the second stage is like the moon on the fifth day; the third stage is like the moon on the eighth day; the fourth stage is like the moon on the ninth day; the fifth stage is like the moon on the tenth day; the sixth stage is like the moon on the eleventh day; the seventh stage is like the moon on the twelfth day; the eighth stage is like the moon on the thirteenth day; the ninth stage is like the moon on the fourteenth day; and the tenth stage is like the moon on the fifteenth day—perfectly visible and fully endowed with luminous characteristics. Their minds are serene, dwelling in immovability; they neither sink nor regress, abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
Once the Bodhisattva has dwelled in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, he is like the Moon Deity, whose palace is made of ten jewels; ten jewel-trees grow forth, with moon-essence maṇi-jewels as their fruit.

By the power of this jewel, the palace of the Moon Deva-son travels throughout Jambudvīpa, universally bestowing coolness; so too it is with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who dwells in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
“Maitreya, you should know that once a bodhisattva-mahāsattva has dwelled in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, they cultivate one hundred gates of samādhi, and only thereafter do they enter the Vajra Samādhi.”
What are the one hundred?
First is the Samādhi of the King of Essential Emptiness; second is the Samādhi of the Ocean of Emptiness; third is the Samādhi of the Realm of Emptiness;
fourth is the Samādhi of the Extinction of the Mind of Emptiness; fifth is the Samādhi of Great Emptiness; sixth is the [Samādhi of] Non-...
1. The samādhi of abiding in the mark of emptiness; 2. The seventh, the samādhi of not perceiving the marks of the mind; 3. The eighth, the samādhi of the wisdom-seal of the mark of emptiness;
4. The ninth, the samādhi of the non-abiding mark of empty space; 5. The tenth, the samādhi of the indestructible mark of the King of Emptiness;
6. The eleventh, the samādhi of the Great Powerful and Valiant King; 7. The twelfth...
The Avataṃsaka Samādhi: Thirteenth, the Samādhi of the King of Light Universally Manifesting Physical Bodies;
Fourteenth, the Sunlight Samādhi; Fifteenth, the Solar Treasury Samādhi; Sixteenth, the Radiant Sunlight Samādhi;
Seventeenth, the Universal Sun Samādhi; Eighteenth, the Collection of Sounds Samādhi.
19. The Samādhi of Silent Radiance; 20. The Samādhi of the Extinction of Objective Marks;
21. The Samādhi of Moving Marks; 22. The Samādhi of Greatly Moving Marks; 23.
The Samādhi of Universally Moving Marks; 24. The Samādhi of Pervasively Moving Marks.
Twenty-fifth is the samādhi of Universal Leaping; twenty-sixth is the samādhi of Universal Roaring;
twenty-seventh is the samādhi of Universal Adornment; twenty-eighth is the samādhi of the Lion’s Mark;
twenty-ninth is the samādhi of the King of Lion’s Power; thirtieth is the samādhi of the King of the Lion’s Roar’s Power.
Thirty-first is the Sun Radiance Samādhi; thirty-second is the Wisdom Torch Samādhi;
thirty-third is the Universal Gate Samādhi; thirty-fourth is the Lotus Treasury Samādhi;
thirty-fifth is the Indestructible Purity Samādhi; thirty-sixth is the Intention of Nirvāṇa Samādhi; thirty-seventh...

Third is the Samādhi of the Illumination of the Dharma-King’s Station; forty-fourth is the Samādhi of the Manifestation of the Dharma-Wheel;
forty-fifth is the Vajra-Treasury Samādhi; forty-sixth is the Vajra-Banner Samādhi;
forty-seventh is the Vajra-Seal Samādhi; forty-eighth is the Vajra-Cluster Samādhi; and so forth.
Nineteenth is the Great Benevolence King Samādhi; fiftieth is the Non-active Benevolence Samādhi;
fifty-first is the Supreme Intention of Great Compassion Samādhi; fifty-second is the Non-abiding Compassionate Aspect Samādhi;
fifty-third is the Solar Orb Radiance Samādhi; fifty-fourth is the Subduing of All Marks through Extinction.
The Samādhi of Subduing All Māras; fifty-fifth, the Samādhi of Victorious Will and Compassion;
fifty-sixth, the Samādhi of Lapis Lazuli Radiance; fifty-seventh, the Samādhi of the Radiance of Seven-Jeweled Fruits;
fifty-eighth, the Samādhi of the Buddha’s Treasury of Accumulations; fifty-ninth, the Samādhi of Supreme Fulfillment of Merit; sixtieth—
Sixty-first is the Samādhi of Expedient Wisdom; sixty-second is the Samādhi of the Markless Wisdom;
sixty-third is the Samādhi of the Ocean-Light of the Buddha; sixty-fourth is the Samādhi of the Universal Ocean;
sixty-fifth is the Samādhi of Oceanic Wisdom; sixty-sixth is the... [not]... [text truncated].

seventy-fourth is the Clever Wisdom Samādhi; seventy-fifth is the Seal-Scripture of All Buddhas Samādhi;
seventy-sixth is the King of Radiance Whose White Light Surges Forth Samādhi; and seventy-seventh is the Purity of Skillful Means and Wisdom.

Regarding the explanation of the samādhis: the ninety-first is the samādhi of the absence of mind and intention;
the ninety-second is the samādhi of the perfection of ethical discipline and wisdom; the ninety-third is the samādhi of the supreme person on the summit;
the ninety-fourth is the samādhi of non-perception through wisdom; the ninety-fifth is the samādhi of severing the twelve [links of dependent origination].
The samādhi of causal conditions; the ninety-sixth is the vajra-light wisdom samādhi;
the ninety-seventh is the mani-flame samādhi; the ninety-eighth is the manifestation of the vajra-seat samādhi;
the ninety-ninth is the power of the roar of the Dharma-wheel king samādhi; and the hundredth is the receiving of the Dharma-king seal samādhi.
“Maitreya, you should know!
These one hundred samādhis are like mani jewels, their radiance illuminating one another, as they enter the ocean of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
Once a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in these one hundred samādhis, his wisdom is like the sun in the sky, while the ocean of all afflictions is like a slight veil of smoke.”
"Maitreya, you should know this!

Just as the great Anavatapta Lake gives rise to four great rivers, and these four great rivers branch into eight, with all the streams of Jambudvīpa eventually returning to the great ocean; and just as the great ocean does not increase because of Mount Vajrārkasandhi, nor does it decrease because of the Vajra-maṇḍala, and because this Vajra-maṇḍala revolves according to the seasons, it causes the waters of the great ocean to have a single salty taste—so too it is with these one hundred samādhis."
Maitreya, you should know this!

Just as when a wheel-turning monarch, by the power of the ten wholesome paths of action, brings forth the seven treasures in response, his precious golden wheel is preeminent in majestic virtue and subdues all universally; his precious jewel satisfies the wishes of sentient beings, granting them their desires without hindrance; and by virtue of his thousand sons, he is formidable and magnificent.
When this Wheel-Turning King wishes to travel, hair grows beneath his feet so that he traverses the void; ten precious lotuses arise to support the King's feet.
"Maitreya, you should know this!

These one hundred samādhis arise from the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the ten pāramitās; they abide securely without departing, yet they do not dwell in quiescent unconditionedness (*asaṃskṛta*), but rather abide on the stage of *jñeyāyatana*.
In this stage of *jñeya*, without cultivation or practice, one will naturally attain eighty-four thousand gateways to samādhi.

These samādhis are indestructible like a mountain of vajra; they ultimately abide at the limit of the great void and likewise enter the signless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). Within all phenomena, one perceives no signs of coming, going, abiding, or ceasing.
With his mind thus tranquil, he immediately attained entry into the Vajra Samādhi.
This Vajra Samādhi is like the Indra-ratna jewel atop the head of the Brahma King: it possesses radiance without manifesting any visible form;
likewise, the Vajra Samādhi does not perceive the ocean of afflictions nor their boundaries.
“Maitreya, you should know this!

Just as the fire-jewel belonging to Īśvara has no form and no marks, yet possesses radiance that is supple and lovely; it can rain down fragrant flowers to satisfy the minds of all devas, and furthermore, it can manifest golden light that outshines the bodily radiance of all other devas.”

Maitreya, you should know that this fire-jewel light is without mind and without consciousness; yet, because it desires to destroy darkness, by the power of the jewel, the darkness is naturally extinguished, and the physical radiance of the various devas becomes twice as bright as usual.

The Vajra-samādhi is also like this: it does not extinguish the fetters, yet the ocean of those fetters dries up of its own accord; it does not sever birth and death, yet the three poisons are extinguished of their own accord.
"Maitreya, you should know this!"
It is like the bright jewel on the forehead of a strongman and the jewel at his elbow, which he constantly conceals with incantations so that others cannot see them.

The great radiance of the Vajra-samādhi remains hidden and tranquil; without seeing the fetters, the mountain of the *anuśayas* collapses of its own accord, without observing the extinction of afflictions, the four great elements cease, the rivers of craving dry up, and the winds of impermanence are severed.
Maitreya, you should know this!
Just as when the lion king roars with full majesty, all wild beasts are naturally subdued and cowed;
so too does the Vajra-samādhi enter and emerge from within śamatha through vipaśyanā, like a vajra sword striking a vajra mountain, leaving no trace behind.

This Vajra-samādhi does not abide and does not arise; it is neither extinguished nor destroyed, neither interrupted nor differentiated, neither liberated nor transformed. It enters the nature of the luminosity of wisdom and gives rise to the profound, wherein the wisdom of the single integrated mark perceives no body, mind, or dharmas; thereafter, one accomplishes Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
This bodhi-wisdom is not separate from non-arising; it is devoid of manifold characteristics and cannot be destroyed, like a mountain of vajra that no one can shake.

The vajra-samādhi neither regresses nor sinks; it enters the state of ultimate great quiescence and sports freely within the ocean of samādhis. By the power of this king of samādhis, all Buddhas and Tathāgatas reach everywhere throughout the entire empty dharma-realm and are able to sport within the abode of noble liberation.
When the Buddha spoke these words, Maitreya Bodhisattva immediately attained the Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas.

At that time, the great assembly of bodhisattvas and others were filled with joy in body and mind; some attained the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, while those who attained the Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas were immeasurable in number.
The Brahmās, Śakras, Lokapālas, and various devaputras rained down celestial flowers and performed manifold musical performances as an offering to the Buddha.
The great assembly, with one voice and in unison, praised Maitreya Bodhisattva:
“Excellent, excellent!”
“Noble son!

You are indeed able to inquire of the Tathāgata regarding such a matter of unsurpassed, great wisdom. Because of you, we have been able to partake of the flavor of the unsurpassed nectar of the Dharma and have attained great and wholesome benefit. We only pray that the Venerable One, on our behalf, will ask: how much merit shall those future sentient beings who hear this Dharma obtain?”
The Buddha addressed the great assembly:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well!
Ninety-one kalpas ago, there was a Buddha, a World-Honored One named Ratnakusuma, who was fully endowed with the ten titles."
At that time, the Buddha Ratnakusuma extensively expounded these hundred gates of samādhi for the sake of the bodhisattvas.

At that assembly, there were a thousand bhikṣus who, upon hearing the World-Honored Buddha preach this samādhi, rejoiced with both body and mind. By the power of the causal conditions of those roots of goodness born of such rejoicing, they transcended the retributions of birth and death for five million billion asaṃkhyeya kalpas.
"Those thousand bhikṣus at that time—were they anyone else?
They are none other than the thousand Buddhas of the present Bhadrakalpa.
The Buddha told the great assembly:

"After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, the eight classes of devas and nāgas, or any others, should even briefly hear of the Buddha’s supreme wisdom, and with deep hearts rejoice in it without giving rise to slander, they shall never fall into the three evil realms for hundreds of thousands of kalpas. In every place where they are born, they will always encounter Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as their kinsmen."

If one hears this Dharma and does not give rise to doubt or slander, after the end of their life they will certainly be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven, where they will encounter Maitreya and hear the exposition of the profound practice of the wheel of Dharma of non-retrogression.

If there are those who uphold, recite, explain, or transcribe [this teaching], and offer various kinds of worship with incense, flowers, and music, when these people approach the end of their lives, if they can mindfully contemplate the Buddha’s Dharma-body with a sincere heart, they will immediately see ninety billion Buddhas come together to extend their hands to them; they shall then be reborn at will in the pure lands of all Buddhas, freely sporting within the ocean of various samādhis.
The Buddha addressed Maitreya and commanded Ānanda:
"You must receive and uphold this well; be careful not to forget or lose it, and until the Dharma is extinguished, you shall propagate and expound it widely.
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One,
what should this sutra be named?
How should we receive and uphold the essentials of this Dharma?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"This sutra is named 'The Ocean of One Hundred Samādhis, Unbreakable and Undying'; it is also named 'The Diamond-like Mark of Quiescent Immovability'; it is also named 'The Sutra on the Innate Purity of the Diamond Samādhi, Unbreakable and Undying. You should uphold it."

When the Buddha had spoken these words, Śāriputra and the other great śrāvakas, Maitreya and the other great bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, were all greatly rejoiced; they prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Vajrasamādhi Spoken by the Buddha, in Which the Innate Nature is Pure, Indestructible, and Unceasing.
